review: 1:3 בִּרְאוֹתְךָ בֵּינֵינוּ — 'when You are seen among us'; the Arabic حِينَ نَرَاكَ وَسْطَنَا is literally 'when we see You', and Hebrew prefers the impersonal passive of seeing, which is the liturgical idiom.
2:1–2:2 אֵין נַפְשֵׁנוּ מוֹצֵאת / נֶחָמָה אֶלָּא בָךְ — the Arabic نُفُوسُنَا لَا تَجِدُ عَزَاهَا إِلَّا فِيك is one sentence split across two lines; Hebrew keeps the split and the negative.
3:3–3:4 בַתְּפִלָּה ... וּבַשִּׁירָה — the Arabic pairs prayer and hymning; the two בְּ prefixes keep the parallel the tune wants.

4:3–4:4 נֵדְעָה דָּבָר פֹּה / מִשִּׂמְחַת שָׁמַיִם — 'we shall know something here of the joy of heaven'; the Arabic سَنَعْرِفُ شَيْئًا هُنَا مِنْ فَرَحِ السَّمَا is deliberately modest, and Hebrew keeps the understatement.
